A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MUFASA study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DINOSAUR-M and SPOT-M segmentation results on VOC, COCO and MOVi-C, alongside efficiency measurements and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original segmentation experiments, efficiency measurements and ablations, and adds further baseline comparisons in appendix Table 7.

M1.justification: The multi-layer slot-attention modules, Hungarian alignment, M-Fusion, mask fusion and training objectives remain unchanged. The new visualization instructions document an existing output procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate unsupervised object segmentation on PASCAL VOC, COCO and MOVi-C. The additional comparisons use these existing datasets without introducing new tasks or test scenarios.

E2.justification: New appendix Table 7 substantially broadens the comparator set: SlotAdapt on VOC and COCO, Multi-Query SA on VOC, FT-DINOSAUR on COCO, and SPOT-FS-RC on all three datasets. Existing comparisons against SA, SLATE, DINOSAUR and SPOT are retained.

E3.justification: The added Table 7 comparison explicitly evaluates FT-DINOSAUR at MUFASA's resolution. Existing dataset splits, training budgets, metrics, preprocessing and test-time ensembling choices remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Layer-selection, fusion-strategy, encoder and decoder ablations are retained, together with the same PCA and qualitative segmentation analyses. The new appendix table supplies benchmark comparisons without adding ablations or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains mean and standard deviation over three seeds. New Table 7 reports three-seed means, consistent with existing mean-only comparison tables; no new run counts, uncertainty procedures or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds comparator scores while retaining MUFASA's results. It reports VOC instance mBO of 51.5 for SlotAdapt versus 51.3 for SPOT-M, and COCO instance mBO of 35.7 for SPOT-FS-RC versus 34.8 for SPOT-M. Existing results otherwise match; Table 2's 12.18-to-12.2-hour edit is equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations (1)-(6) retain the same content. Neither version introduces additional theorems, proofs or formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: multi-layer slot fusion, plug-and-play integration, improved segmentation, faster convergence and SOTA performance. The added comparisons do not revise these headline claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 newly identifies one-to-one Hungarian alignment as a potential constraint and suggests soft matching. Appendix D contextualizes comparisons through competitors' additional training signals and caption-based pretraining; the existing instance-grouping limitation remains.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.2 explains bilinear upsampling, per-pixel slot assignment, coloring and image overlays. The project address changes and is explicitly labeled as providing code. Existing hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work expands to cover multi-query slot attention, GLASS, motion-refined DINOSAUR, and multi-layer approaches to forecasting, correspondence and object discovery. Appendix D adds positioning against newer competitors, while the central novelty claim remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes local wording and terminology edits, expands acknowledgments, adds brief appendix sections, and separates appendix references. The main narrative and section organization are largely preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds comparison Table 7, relocates the former hyperparameter Table 7 as Table 8, and adjusts appendix caption placement and pagination. The ten existing figures and their substantive visual content are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional comparisons, clearer research positioning, matching limitation and visualization instructions modestly improve completeness and transparency. The method and original experimental evidence remain stable. The gain is limited by unchanged broad SOTA wording despite Table 7 reporting competitors with higher instance mBO on VOC and COCO, although Appendix D acknowledges differences in training resources.
